Welcome to Queen's Park Infant Academy
May I extend a warm welcome to Queens Park Infant Academy. It really is a very special place. We are a three-form infant school located in Charminster, Bournemouth, where the success of every child matters to us.
We believe that the first years of school are the most important years of a child's life - and should certainly be the most exciting! Our dedicated and talented team of staff are committed to providing the very best education possible, with a strong focus on developing the foundational skills within our children (early reading, writing, mathematics, communication and self-regulation). We love being part of the children’s learning journey and pride ourselves on strong, positive relationships with our families.
We are always delighted to show parents and children around our school and welcome new families to our community. If you would like to visit the school, please telephone the office to make an appointment.

Coastal Learning Partnership
Thank you for taking an interest in Queen's Park Infant Academy, which is a highly valued member of the Multi Academy Trust, Coastal Learning Partnership (CLP).
CLP is a single family of twenty schools across two Local Authority areas: Dorset Council and Bournemouth, Christchurch & Poole Council. The two furthermost points of CLP are Boscombe and Swanage. There are about 5,400 pupils overall who are supported by around 900 committed staff.
Our schools work closely together in a spirit of professional generosity and collaboration, sharing resource and expertise.
Although part of the same single family, every school in CLP is different and unique and those differences are greatly valued. Each school has its own identify and values which express the local communities that they serve. Those schools within CLP which are church schools express their Christian distinctiveness through their unique vision.
CLP’s motto is ‘Broadening Horizons Together’. This is because we want every member of the CLP community to really flourish; children enjoy an inspiring educational experience and staff enjoy professional opportunity and fulfilment. That is achieved through being part of a single learning community.
CLP has three core values which influence the way in which we work together:
Queen's Park Infant Academy has made a commitment to the CLP family, secure in the knowledge that serving others in this way will lead to a better educational experience for all of the pupils.
If you would like to learn more about the work of the Partnership and its other schools, or to view documentation such as statutory accounts, please visit the Coastal Learning Partnership website.
You can contact Coastal Learning Partnership directly as follows:
Email: office@coastalpartnership.co.uk Call: 01202 806155 Write: Coastal Learning Partnership Heathlands Primary Academy Andrews Close Springwater Road Bournemouth, Dorset BH11 8HB

Kinetic Letters
The Kinetic Letters program is commenced in EYFS and is used throughout the school. Handwriting sessions are taught to the whole class, with differentiated targets where needed. Additional handwriting and fine and gross motor skills interventions may take place for some children.
The underlying principles of Kinetic Letters
As part of this we have been doing lots of activities that will make our bodies stronger for writing. You could try some of these activities at home as well!
Once the children learn to form the letters, they hear stories about Bounce (brave monkey) and Skip (scared monkey) who help them to know where to start their letters. We use special whiteboards to give the children a prompt to remember this.
Ask your child about Bounce and Skip to find out more!
What are the Kinetic Letter Families?
Each of the families are introduced to the children through stories. The children are also introduced to Bounce and Skip the monkeys when reading these stories.
The Jumper Family Story
Bounce and Skip spend all day jumping down - bump from the branches of their tree!
Bounce jumps from the high branch and makes the letter trail for h and b.
Skip jumps from the low branch and makes the letter trail for r, n, m and p.
But....when Skip jumps down to make p, he gets a surprise! Instead of going bump, he falls on down into a pit that has a spider!
He jumps back up, pushing the cobwebs off to make the p letter trail!
The Abracadabra Family Story
Scared monkey Skip finds a magician who waves his wand and shouts 'Abracadabra' and makes lots of different letters appear under the lower branch of the tree.
The magician teaches Skip the magic trick. He shows him that for each of the letters, he can pull around to write c, shout 'Abracadabra' and then magic it into o, a, d, g, q or s.
Skip makes all the letters start from his branch.
The Window Cleaner Family Story
The Monkeys find themselves in a city standing by a shop window! They watch two window cleaners making marks as they dry the windows. The pull the squeegees down the windows and flick the water off at the bottom!
The window cleaners let the Brave Monkey climb the ladder, pull the squeegee down the window, bump the ground and flick the water off! This makes a l and the t.
Scared Monkey is nervous about climbing the ladder so he stays on the ground and makes an i and u.
The Slider Family Story
One exciting day the magician waves his wand and takes Brave Monkey and Scared Monkey to see the snow!
Skip the Scared Monkey finds a snowy mountain slope and says 'I can slide down and slide up'. When he does this, he can make the letters v, w, x and z.
Bounce the Brave Monkey goes to help the baby penguins who have lost their beaks! The penguins stand in line whilst the monkey fixes them back on and this makes the k!
The Special Squirter Story
A big storm has flooded the pit under the monkeys' tree. The mole rats are upset, as this is where they live.
First Skip rescues the fish that have been washed into the pit. Next he asks the elephant to help by sucking the water up into his trunk and squirting it back into the river.
Skip helps by holding the trunk and squirting it under his branch, leaving a letter trail of water behind in the air!
The Fisher Family Story
One day there is a huge storm in the jungle which makes the river flood the spider's pit. Bounce the Brave Monkey and Skip the Scared Monkey sit in their tree and watch the fish swim around in the pit. Skip discovers that if he sits on his branch and dangles his tail in the water, he can pull his tail around to catch the fish!

Pets as Therapy Dog
Ru – Our Pets as Therapy Dog
QPIA is registered with Pets as Therapy, and we are so lucky to have Ru (and her owner Karen) as part of our school team.
Ru comes to school regularly. She sometimes visits assemblies, but most often is found listening to stories. It’s called the ‘Read 2 Dogs’ programme (you can find out more about Pets as Therapy and Read 2 Dogs by clicking here).
This is Ru with Karen, her owner......
Most of the children will see Ru, but he will only work 1:1 with a few children each term. This is managed by Mrs Parker, our Family Support Worker.

pageCache.pageTitle: Queen's Park Infant Academy - Vision & Values
pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
Queen's Park Infant Academy Motto
A happy school, learning, caring, succeeding together.
Our passionate vision is to create an inclusive, nurturing school, which excites a love of learning. A school, which promotes high expectations, recognises achievement and celebrates success in all areas of development for all children.
At Queen's Park Infant Academy we know that every child is an individual with unique talents and we aim to foster these. We teach our children to take proactive responsibility for thinking about their own learning and thinking about how to learn together. We aim to develop resilient, self-aware life long learners.
Together in partnership we can nurture and encourage confident, caring, independent children. Children who enjoy learning and who always believe that they can achieve more tomorrow than they have today.
Our values are presented in a way that our children can easily understand and explain. Each of our 4 'bees' is characterised by its image, and each bee has a set of descriptors that help us express what each value looks and sounds like in action.

pageCache.text:
Bee Happy After School Club
(3.10PM – 5.30PM MONDAY – FRIDAY)
"My daughter is loving after school club. She said it’s so much fun and you’re all kind and friendly. She’s told me and her dad to stop picking her up too early from after school club because she wants to stay until the end. It’s so good to know she is happy, thank you."
"Thank you for the care, kindness and warmth you've shown both of our children over the past 5 years.You've created a space where our children feel safe, happy and excited to be. As working parents, we simply couldn't have done it without you. Your care and support has allowed us to maintain our careers, knowing our girls were in the best hands. We will always be grateful for the part you've all played in our family journey."
"Thank you for providing a lovely after school experience for my daughter. It has really helped her to gain in confidence."
"Thank you for being kind, nurturing and fun and playing games with our children. It's wonderful to know you're there for our children to enable us to continue working. Bee Happy is a wonderful environment for our children to thrive."
"Thank you all so much for the years of fantastic care that you have provided for both our daughters. We have been so lucky to have you give them a homely space where they have felt safe and enjoyed their time."
Children are collected from their classrooms at the end of the school day. Bee Happy closes at 5.30pm.
We offer a range of board games, puzzles and card games for the children to use. We have a role play area with a shop, kitchen and other imaginative play equipment, along with some dressing up clothes.
We have cars and track, garages, dolls and prams, Lego and construction toys, arts and crafts, painting and colouring. Plenty to engage and entertain our children!
We provide a snack, typically bread or crackers with butter and either jam, lemon curd, honey or marmite and a drink of water or squash. Fruit is also available.
During the warmer months we also have access to an outdoor area where children can play games or just enjoy being with their friends.
Be Happy is run by our own school staff, and works within our whole school policies. Miss Pauline Abel is the manager. She is First Aid trained and is our Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) on site for Bee Happy.
Bee Happy costs £9 per session, or part thereof. This incudes a snack and a drink.
Bee Happy accepts Childcare Vouchers (EdenRed, Care4, Co-operative Flexible Benefits) and is part of the Government Tax Free Childcare Scheme. Please advise Miss Abel in advance of booking if you intend to use either of these.
If you are interested in your child attending Bee Happy, please contact Miss Pauline Abel by email on
bee.happy@coastalpartnership.co.uk
Please include your child’s name and class. You will then be sent details of how to book sessions.
IMPORTANT INFORMATION FOR PARENTS OF CHILDREN ATTENDING BEE HAPPY
Contact Miss Abel on bee.happy@coastalpartnership.co.uk for all enquiries relating to Bee Happy.
The mobile number for Bee Happy is 07999 714100. It is important that you store this number in your phone contacts.
Collecting your Child
Collection from Bee Happy is via the bottom blue gate, where the bike sheds are. You must telephone Miss Abel on 07999 714100 to advise her that you have arrived. We will bring your child out to you. You can collect any time up until 5.30pm.
If your Child is Attending Another Club After School
If your child attends a sports / dance or choir club on a day they are also booked into Bee Happy, it is important to tell both Miss Abel and the club leader. Children will them be brought to Bee Happy after the club has finished.
If you arrive after 5.35pm on more than 2 occasions, you will no longer be able to have a credit for cancelling a future session during the current term.
If late collection persists, we have the right to withdraw after school care for our child/ren.
Please email Bee Happy by 9am on the day of the session if your child is not going to attend. This will then allow us to offer the space to another child and your account can be credited. If we are not advised by 9am, the session will be charged for.
Please not, the mobile number is not accessed until 3pm, so cancellations must be done via email.
It is important to advise Miss Abel via email every time a payment has been made. Please include the date sent, payment amount and, if applicable, the voucher provider.
